subject: geography
title: How Volcanoes Form
welcome_lead: Earth's surface bubbles and bursts! Discover how volcanoes form and why they appear where they do.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on volcano formation and plate boundaries.
final_note: Brilliant! You now understand how volcanoes form.

walkthroughs.body_html: Below the crust, hot rock can melt into magma. It rises through cracks and weak spots. When it reaches the surface, we call it lava.
Most volcanoes form at destructive or constructive plate boundaries. The Pacific Ring of Fire hosts about 75% of the world's volcanoes!
Some volcanoes (like Hawaii) form over hot spots — plumes of magma rising from deep within Earth, even in the middle of plates.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes typically cause more deaths in LICs than HICs?
options: Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.
LICs often have poorly enforced building codes, weak emergency response, dense informal housing and limited preparedness — not because the earthquakes are stronger.
LICs have more earthquake deaths because more earthquakes happen there.

mcqs.q: How are fold mountains like the Himalayas formed?
options: Fold mountains form when one plate slides under another into the mantle.
Fold mountains form from giant volcanoes erupting upwards.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.
By the collision of two continental plates (India and Eurasia) where neither can subduct, so the crust crumples and is forced upwards over millions of years.
